investigation.method: manual review of the live website with NHS profile and selected repo evidence

headline: Pennine Surgery is a useful reminder that PATCHS is not automatically a bad signal. The public site is a clear My Surgery Website build, PATCHS is framed as the route for non-urgent contact, NHS App is used for appointments and records, and the surrounding copy is much calmer and clearer than on the low-performing My Surgery Website case reviewed so far.

live_stack.label: Public website stack
evidence: The footer says Built by My Surgery Website.
Response headers set an msw practice code cookie.

live_stack.label: Current online request platform for non-urgent contact
evidence: The homepage and online-services page link to https://patchs.ai/practice/penninesurgery/.
The homepage says PATCHS can be used for anything non-urgent, including appointment requests and cancellations.

live_stack.label: Prescription-side legacy platform
evidence: The prescriptions page lists EMIS Access alongside NHS App, paper requests and email.
That means Pennine still exposes more than one digital route for repeat medication.

current_routes.label: PATCHS direct route
notes: The site presents PATCHS as the route for non-urgent requests, appointment requests and appointment amendments.
The homepage says the practice may respond with phone, video or face-to-face follow-up if needed.

current_routes.label: NHS App route
current_routes.kind: app-mediated access for appointments, prescriptions and records
notes: The online-services page says patients can book and cancel appointments and view records using the NHS App.
The site treats NHS App as a first-class route, not just a footer mention.

current_routes.label: Appointments workflow
notes: Urgent needs are said to be handled within 24 hours.
Routine appointments are said to be offered within 14 days.
The page says routine appointments may be telephone or face-to-face and that home visit requests are assessed by callback.

current_routes.label: Prescriptions
notes: The page offers NHS App, EMIS Access, a paper request form and email.
It says repeat prescriptions are not taken over the phone unless the patient is housebound.
It also offers PATCHS for non-urgent queries and tells patients to phone the pharmacist after 10am.

complaints_and_feedback.headline: Pennine has a live complaints area, but it is weaker than the access pages and leans heavily on feedback tooling.

items.label: Feedback and complaints hub
notes: The main page is largely framed around feedback and Friends and Family content.
A stronger complaints route exists one click deeper on the leave-feedback page.

items.label: Complaints form guidance
notes: The page says medical matters and official complaints cannot be handled through the suggestions form.
It separately says patients should complete the complaints form so the practice manager can deal with the concern.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: PATCHS is broad but not the whole front door
notes: Pennine talks about PATCHS as a wide non-urgent route, but urgent and some same-day handling still appears to depend on staff contact and callback.

gpps_2025_26.headline: Pennine is extremely strong on contact measures as well as overall satisfaction.

google_review_texts.headline: The captured review sample is consistently positive about staff helpfulness, prompt action and actually being seen.
notes: Several reviews praise reception staff by name and describe quick practical help.
The tone is notably about responsiveness and kindness rather than slick digital tooling.

probably_true: Pennine performs well because its routes are clear and layered rather than because PATCHS itself is special.
This is a high-performing contrast case against Inspire, which uses a similar website supplier and PATCHS but presents a much harsher access experience.
needs_follow_up: Whether the complaints form on the leave-feedback page is a true embedded form or mostly guidance text.
How much demand is still being pulled back to phone despite the broad PATCHS wording.
